evidence.excerpt: Constructive nesting heuristics require hand-crafted placement rules whose performance varies substantially across polygon types. This paper investigates whether a graph neural network (GNN) can learn a placement policy from solved instances, replacing the manual rule. Each partial layout is represented as a graph in which nodes encode piece geometric features (area, perimeter, convexity ratio) and edges encode spatial relationships between already-placed pieces and the candidate piece. The GNN is trained on 4,800 solved instances generated from the CEE benchmark dataset using a supervised imitation-learning objective. On a held-out test set of 400 instances, the GNN-guided heuristic achieves average utilisation of 82.1% compared to 79.4% for the best constructive baseline, at comparable computation time. Generalisation experiments on ESICUP instances not seen during training show a 1.2 percentage-point improvement over baseline, suggesting transferability. The approach requires approximately 14 hours of training on a single GPU; inference time per placement decision is under 3 milliseconds.
